claims.text: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹.
HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance that limits high-temperature use in air.
An anti-oxidation coating is an appropriate intervention for high-temperature use of HfNbTaTiZr in air.
A thin alumina-forming coating can be deposited as a continuous, adherent layer on cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The deposited coating will form a continuous, thermally stable alumina surface layer during high-temperature exposure.
The coating will develop into a dense and adherent Al2O3 scale at approximately 1000 °C in air.
The Al2O3 scale will greatly retard oxygen diffusion into the HfNbTaTiZr substrate.
Retarding oxygen ingress will limit oxidation-induced degradation of the substrate.
Limiting oxygen ingress will preserve the bulk microstructure responsible for the alloy's mechanical performance.
After exposure near 1000 °C in air for tens to approximately 100 hours, coated samples will have lower oxidation weight gain than uncoated samples.
After the specified exposure, coated samples will have thinner oxide scales than uncoated samples.
The coating will preserve room-temperature tensile ductility at a level similar to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The coating will preserve high-temperature yield strength at a level similar to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr under strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹.
Untreated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr undergoes high-temperature oxidation that degrades its mechanical performance.
The proposed coating is expected to be effective under relatively steady exposure around 1000 °C.
